data.title: Singapore and World Bank ink 3-year partnership targeting power trade gaps
data.description:
The deal covers capacity building and knowledge sharing for members.

The Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry, the Ministry of Finance (MOF), and the World Bank Group have launched a three-year ASEAN Power Grid Mobilisation Partnership (AMP) between Singapore and the World Bank.

The partnership will support cross-border electricity trade by strengthening regulatory, institutional and financing frameworks, including arrangements for cross-border wheeling, the groups said.

It will also promote regional cooperation, capacity building, and knowledge sharing amongst ASEAN member states.

Alvin Lim, MOF director-general, said the AMP will enable the region’s energy transition, address gaps in project implementation, and improve project bankability.

data.title: Keppel DC REIT buys 88.62% stake in two Japan data centres
data.description:
The acquisition was partly funded by proceeds from a $625m private placement.

Keppel DC REIT has bought an 88.62% effective interest in two data centres in Inzai City, Japan, Keppel DC REIT Management Pte. Ltd said.

Keppel used $617.5m from a $625m private placement on 2 September to partly fund the acquisition.

Of the proceeds, $7.5m went to the estimated fees and expenses, including professional fees.

About $1.7m originally allocated for fees was reallocated to partially fund the acquisition, Keppel said.

The acquisition follows Keppel’s 1 September announcement on the deal and its 2 September announcement on the private placement results.

As of 1 October, the $625m proceeds from the private placement have been fully utilised, Keppel DC REIT said in a bourse filing.

data.title: Westholme marks 10 years in Singapore with a dinner shaped by fire
data.description:
Australia's finest Wagyu meets Australia's finest fire, as Firedoor chef Lennox Hastie arrives in Singapore for the first time.

Ten years ago, Westholme entered Singapore quietly, finding its way into the city’s kitchens through chefs who valued consistency, provenance and flavour. On 15 September, the Australian Wagyu producer, renowned for its premium quality and nature-led approach to raising cattle, celebrated its first decade in the market with an intimate anniversary dinner at Ida’s in Gillman Barracks.

At the centre of the evening was Chef Lennox Hastie, the chef and owner of Sydney’s acclaimed, Firedoor, where wood fire is the sole source of heat for cooking.

A longtime Westholme advocate, Hastie has travelled internationally to share a deceptively simple proposition with chefs and diners: exceptional beef, understood through fire. The dinner marked his first visit to Singapore, with travel supported by Qantas, bringing one of Australia’s most distinctive culinary voices to a market that has helped shape Westholme’s international story.

The event came as live-fire cooking continues to move into the global restaurant mainstream. The MICHELIN Guide named “char, smoke and flame” among the defining food trends of 2026, highlighting chefs working with embers, wood, hot stones and charcoal from Stockholm to Buenos Aires and China.

For Hastie, whose kitchen at Firedoor operates without gas or electricity for cooking, “Fire is the ultimate lie detector,” because wood fire is the instrument through which ingredients are tested and revealed.

He continues, “Westholme’s unique flavour becomes more pronounced through live fire, and its even marbling melts and caramelises cleanly. There aren’t any shortcuts in how its cattle are raised or how we cook it. It’s just beef, salt and fire, so the product has to be honest.” 

Westholme is owned and operated by the Australian Agricultural Company, founded in 1824 and Australia’s oldest continuously operating company. That heritage of more than 200 years informs Westholme’s approach to raising Wagyu across the ancient rangelands of northern Australia, combining selective breeding with animal wellbeing and long-term stewardship of the land.

The anniversary dinner brought together approximately 50 chefs, customers, tastemakers and industry partners. The evening explored the relationships between land and flavour, farmer and chef, and Australia and Singapore.

Nowhere is that bond clearer than on the city’s own menus. Over the past decade, Westholme has found its way onto tables with markedly different culinary identities, including Empire Grill at Raffles Sentosa Singapore, Magpie in Tiong Bahru and SUSHISAMBA at Capital Tower - a range that speaks to the product's versatility and the partnerships Westholme has cultivated along the way.

“Singapore’s chefs have been among Westholme’s most discerning advocates since we entered the market,” said Andrew O’Brien, Westholme’s Chief Commercial Officer. “This anniversary is both a thank you and a statement of intent. We want to deepen our relationships with the people who have built the brand alongside us and create a stronger, more direct conversation about what goes into producing exceptional Australian beef.”

For a brand that has spent 10 years earning its place one kitchen at a time, the next decade begins in much the same way: around a table, with the product speaking through the people who know it best.

data.title: OCBC Securities sees 60% trade spike from young investors
data.description:
OCBC Securities sees 60% trade spike from young investors

OCBC Securities’ saw a 60% spike in trades by investors aged 30 years old and younger as of 30 September 2026.

Active young investors in OCBC Securities rose over 20% year-on-year (YoY) over the same period, outpacing growth across the bank’s wider investor base, according to OCBC.

OCBC expects momentum to continue due to the SGX’s upcoming reduction of board lot size from 100 units to 10 units for instruments priced above S$10, and from 100 units to 1 unit for instruments priced above S$100. The reduction kicks off on 5 October 2026.

“Younger investors have historically traded in smaller amounts and are overwhelmingly digital, making the upcoming changes to the board lot size particularly relevant to them,” said Wilson He, managing director, OCBC Securities.

OCBC Securities said ti will permanently remove minimum commissions for all online trades on SGX beginning 5 October.

More than 95% of OCBC Securities’ young investor base trade exclusively only, the bank said.

“Our permanent removal of minimum commission on SGX online trades gives them even more flexibility to trade in smaller amounts,” He said.

He also expects the removal of minimum commissions and smaller board lot sizes to benefit other segments. Clients should find it easier to sell odd lots, accumulated through scrip dividend schemes where dividends are paid in shares rather than cash, according to He.

data.title: STI ends September at 5,675.88, down 1.4%
data.description:
Katrina Group was the month's strongest performer.

The Straits Times Index (STI) ended September at 5,675.88, down 1.4% for the month, after hitting a record 5,828.5 on 4 September.

The two STI exchange-traded funds, the SPDR STI ETF and the Amova STI ETF, drew net inflows of $293m in September.

Meanwhile, the FTSE ST Catalist Index rose 2.4%, led by iX Biopharma, up 25.9% after a US Government declaration opened an emergency-use pathway for its Wafermine drug.

The stock now makes up 19% of the index, up from about 5% in March. The FTSE ST All-Share Technology Index gained 1.7%, whilst the FTSE ST REIT Index fell 5.7%.

Katrina Group was the month's strongest performer amongst about 180 actively traded stocks, surging 270% after a BYD-linked dealer acquired a 5% stake for about $300,000.

Accrelist followed with a 39.3% gain.

Institutional investors were net sellers of about  $1.02b, whilst retail investors bought about $1.13b.

Institutions favoured utilities, with about  $106m of net inflows led by Sembcorp Industries, and technology, with about $81m led by AEM.

They sold financial services, REITs, real estate excluding REITs and telecommunications, which retail investors bought.

Meanwhile, non-oil domestic exports rose 46.2% year on year in August, and industrial production grew 15.4%.

The median private-sector forecast for 2026 gross domestic product growth in the Monetary Authority of Singapore's September survey rose to 5.0% from 3.5% in June, with 3.1% projected for 2027.

data.title: Coliwoo proposes $45.8m sale, leaseback of River Valley properties
data.description:
Deal covers 50 co-living rooms across the two properties.

Coliwoo Holdings Limited has proposed the sale and leaseback of two co-living properties at 298 River Valley Road and 288 River Valley Road for an aggregate consideration of $45.8m.

The Singapore-listed co-living operator said it entered into two put and call option agreements on 30 September 2026 with Qing Feng Construction Pte Ltd to sell its entire shareholding in Coliwoo RV1 Pte. Ltd. and Coliwoo RV2 Pte. Ltd., which wholly own the properties.

Following completion, Coliwoo will lease the properties back for three years and continue operating all 50 rooms under the Coliwoo brand. The company said this will allow it to retain operational control and maintain business continuity.

The transaction is subject to completion conditions, including shareholders’ approval at an extraordinary general meeting and relevant regulatory approvals. Completion is expected in the financial year ending 30 September 2027.

The properties are freehold shophouses that Coliwoo acquired and converted into co-living spaces, with 13 rooms at 298 River Valley Road and 37 rooms at 288 River Valley Road, alongside street-level commercial units.

Coliwoo acquired 298 River Valley Road in April 2022, while it acquired 286 and 288 River Valley Road in October 2023. The latter two properties have since been amalgamated as 288 River Valley Road.

The proposed sale and leaseback forms part of Coliwoo’s capital recycling programme, following the sale and leaseback of Coliwoo Hotel Pasir Panjang in January 2026 and Coliwoo Midtown, which was completed on 30 September 2026.

The company said the transaction will allow it to unlock capital from stabilised assets and redeploy funds into higher-yielding growth opportunities.

The S$45.8m consideration was negotiated on an arm’s-length, willing-buyer, willing-seller basis, taking into account the independent valuation of the properties, the net assets of the target companies, debt to be settled at completion and the leaseback terms.

After repaying borrowings on the properties and settling transaction expenses and other completion adjustments, Coliwoo expects to receive net cash proceeds of approximately S$18.7m.

The company plans to use the proceeds for general corporate and working capital purposes, including funding existing and future projects and reducing debt.

Although the consideration exceeds Coliwoo’s original acquisition cost and related acquisition expenses, the transaction is expected to result in a non-cash accounting fair value loss in FY2026.

This is because the $45.8m consideration is below the carrying value of the properties as at 31 March 2026, which includes fair value gains recognised in prior periods.

Coliwoo said the illustrative reduction in net tangible assets and earnings per share disclosed in its announcement is primarily attributable to the non-cash accounting adjustment and transaction-related expenses.

The company expects the proposed sale and leaseback to strengthen its balance sheet and provide additional capital for future growth opportunities.

data.title: Jardine Matheson acquires Australia’s I-MED Radiology Network
data.description:
Deal marks Jardines’ first major investment since 2025.

Jardine Matheson Holdings (Jardines) has completed the acquisition of I-MED Radiology Network (I-MED), an Australia-based diagnostic imaging and teleradiology provider.

The acquisition marks Jardines’ first major investment since it transitioned to an investment company in 2025.

Jardines said the investment will form a new earnings growth pillar for the group and is aligned with its strategy of being an Asia Pacific-focused control owner of high-quality, scalable businesses.

The deal also supports the 2030 objectives outlined at Jardines’ Investor Day in June.

As part of the transaction, Jardines will work closely with I-MED’s management team to support the company’s continued growth and expansion.

Lincoln Pan, CEO of Jardine Matheson, said the company is partnering with I-MED’s doctors and clinicians, whom he described as key to the radiology practice’s position in Australia. "I-MED is a trusted leader in radiology, with a long history of clinical excellence and a deep network of partners in its medical communities.”

data.title: HDB resale market may stabilise after 3 quarters of decline
data.description:
Private home prices will likely remain resilient.

Property analysts expect Singapore’s private-home prices to remain resilient despite lower transaction volumes, whilst the HDB resale market could stabilise after prices declined for a third consecutive quarter.

Private residential prices rose 1.4% QoQ in Q3 2026, up from 0.5% in the previous quarter. Prices rose 2.8% during the first nine months of the year.

The increase was led by landed homes, where prices rose 2.8%. Non-landed prices increased 0.9%, supported by a 2.2% gain in the Outside Central Region.

Prices in the Rest of Central Region edged up 0.2%, whilst those in the Core Central Region declined 0.1%.

Huttons Asia CEO Mark Yip said landed homes were the main driver of the quarterly increase, whilst new projects helped establish higher price benchmarks in the suburban market.

However, private-home transaction volume fell about 30% to 4,296 units, based on transactions recorded through mid-September.

Yip attributed the decline partly to fewer launches during the seventh lunar month, affordability concerns and buyers taking time to assess recent housing-policy changes.

Huttons estimated that developers launched and sold approximately 1,100 new private homes during the quarter. It expects around 7,000 units to be sold for the full year, with private-home prices increasing by 3% to 4%.

Knight Frank Singapore Head of Research Leonard Tay said landed prices continued to reach new highs despite relatively stable quarterly sales volumes.

He said demand remained supported by homeowners seeking to upgrade from apartments to landed properties.

The removal of the 15-month wait-out period for private-property owners buying non-subsidized HDB resale flats could also increase transactions by encouraging retirees to sell larger private homes and right-size, Tay added.

Knight Frank expects private-home price growth to finish near the middle of its 3% to 5% full-year forecast.

However, Tay warned that rising retrenchments and uncertainty surrounding artificial intelligence’s effects on employment could prompt potential buyers to delay major purchases.

Cushman & Wakefield Head of Research for Singapore and Southeast Asia Wong Xian Yang said Q3’s faster price increase may have been partly influenced by lower transaction volumes and differences in the price points of newly launched projects.

Higher-priced launches could raise overall sales prices even as the number of transactions declines.

Wong expects private-home prices to rise by 3% to 4% in 2026, supported by underlying local demand, borrowing costs and higher replacement costs.

However, he described an emerging tug of war in which buyers are taking longer to decide whilst sellers continue to hold their asking prices. This could result in lower transaction volumes but continued modest price gains.

The HDB resale market showed a different trend. Prices fell 0.2% QoQ and 0.6% YoY in Q3, marking a third consecutive quarterly decline.

Resale volume nevertheless increased 5.2% from a year earlier to 7,528 units.

Realion Chief Researcher and Strategist Christine Sun said removing the 15-month wait-out period generated more inquiries from private homeowners seeking to right-size, although stronger interest has not yet fully translated into completed transactions.

She expects demand for larger resale flats and million-dollar units to increase as private homeowners sell their properties and move into more affordable public housing.

However, Sun said premium transactions remained too small a share of the market to cause a broad price surge.

An increasing supply of flats reaching their minimum occupation period and the higher income ceilings for new HDB flats could also restrain resale-price growth by giving buyers more alternatives, she added.

data.title: Gov’t studying fusion as potential clean-energy pathway
data.description:
The METI places greater emphasis on energy security, economic growth and climate resilience.

Singapore is studying nuclear fusion as a potential low-carbon energy pathway as the new Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry (METI) places greater emphasis on energy security, economic growth and climate resilience.

The Ministry of Trade and Industry formally became METI on 1 October, reflecting the growing importance of energy to Singapore’s economic competitiveness and long-term resilience.

Speaking at FusionX 2026, Minister for Energy, Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry) Tan See Leng said energy was an essential resource requiring long-term planning.

He said global developments had strengthened the need for Singapore to study emerging energy technologies and leave no potential pathway unexplored.

Fusion energy is one option the country is monitoring closely, although commercially operating fusion power plants could still be years away. Singapore has not decided whether to deploy any form of nuclear energy.

Fusion generates energy by combining atomic nuclei under extreme heat and pressure, unlike nuclear fission, which splits atoms.

The technology could produce lower levels of radioactive waste and has a limited risk of runaway reactions, but maintaining stable fusion conditions and achieving a net-positive energy return remain major technical challenges.

Singapore’s exploration of fusion forms part of its wider effort to diversify its energy sources and achieve net-zero emissions by 2050.

The country has increased its solar deployment target to 3 gigawatt-peak by 2030 after reaching its previous 2 GWp target ahead of schedule. It is also pursuing regional low-carbon electricity imports and studying the possible deployment of nuclear fission.

Singapore will participate in the International Atomic Energy Agency’s Integrated Nuclear Infrastructure Review in 2027 to assess its readiness to make an informed decision on nuclear fission.

Even without constructing a fusion reactor, Singapore could participate in the industry through its expertise in precision engineering, advanced manufacturing, plasma diagnostics and deep technology.

A*STAR has worked with US-based Realta Fusion since 2025 to develop a diagnostic tool that measures plasma velocities, helping researchers understand and control conditions within fusion systems.

The agency and Realta Fusion are exploring further collaboration in advanced plasma diagnostics and deployment.

SGInnovate and consulting firm Helixos have identified materials and coatings, plasma-facing components, diagnostics, software and control systems as potential areas for Singapore to enter the global fusion value chain.
